Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Horizon Financial Group Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, ladies and gentlemen, this conference is being recorded. In order to ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. We will pause momentarily to compile the Q&A roster.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Lisa Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Lisa Thompson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review Horizon Financial Group's results for the third quarter. With me this morning are John Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Patel, Chief Risk Officer; David Wong, Chief Credit Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and Robert Kline, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to John Reynolds.

John Reynolds:
Thank you, Lisa, and good morning, everyone. Horizon Financial Group delivered exceptional results in the third quarter, exceeding expectations and demonstrating the strength of our diversified business model.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on accelerating revenue growth, improving profitability, managing risk effectively, investing in technology and innovation, enhancing customer experience, strengthening our brand, and delivering value to our shareholders.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on our progress across critical areas. First, on key strategic initiatives, we've advanced our Forward 2027 plan through digital transformation, customer personalization, and sustainable growth, with cloud migrations cutting costs and AI tools boosting efficiency. Second, revenue diversification efforts have lifted non-interest income to 42% of total revenue via wealth management, payments, and capital markets growth. Third, our macroeconomic outlook sees global GDP at 3.2% for 2024, with Fed cuts supporting consumer strength despite CRE and geopolitical risks. Fourth, credit quality metrics show NPL ratios at a low 98 basis points, down sequentially, with strong coverage across segments. Fifth, provisions for credit losses totaled $450 million, driven by consumer and CRE pressures but backed by robust CECL modeling. Sixth, capital ratios are solid with CET1 at 13.2%, well above regulatory needs including G-SIB surcharges. And seventh, net interest income rose strongly, with guidance pointing to continued expansion next quarter.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, John, and good morning. Horizon Financial Group reported net income of $1.2 billion for the third quarter, or $2.45 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 12% year-over-year driven by higher loan balances and improved deposit mix. Non-interest income was up 15%, reflecting strong performance in wealth management and trading. Our capital ratios remain strong, and we are well-positioned to support future growth.

Diving deeper into net interest income, which forms the foundation of our earnings, we achieved $2.52 billion in the quarter, a 9% increase from last year and 4% from the prior quarter, surpassing consensus estimates. This was powered by earning assets averaging $285 billion, up 6% year-over-year, with loan growth particularly in commercial and industrial sectors like technology and renewables. Consumer lending grew steadily through fintech partnerships that lowered funding costs. Deposits averaged $240 billion, with core low-cost deposits at 52% of the mix, and betas stabilizing amid competition from high-yield alternatives.

Regionally, U.S. operations generated the bulk at $1.78 billion, up 12% on NIM expansion to 3.65%, while Europe and Asia-Pacific contributed solid growth from mortgage portfolios and wealth-linked lending. Initiatives like securities repositioning and AI-driven pricing added meaningful basis points to our NIM of 3.52%.

For the fourth quarter, we guide NII to $2.60 billion to $2.70 billion, with core NIM at 3.55% to 3.65%, assuming stable Fed rates, modest loan growth, and easing deposit betas. Adjusted EPS is expected at $1.85 to $1.98, supported by fee growth and expense control, with efficiency ratio at 55-56%. This includes provisions around $450-500 million and capital returns via buybacks and a dividend increase.

Turning to capital, our CET1 ratio reached 13.2% fully loaded, up 40 basis points quarter-over-quarter, with Tier 1 at 15.4%. These exceed requirements like the 10.7% total CET1 need including buffers and G-SIB surcharge, and position us ahead of peers. Drivers include retained earnings from 14.2% ROE and RWA optimization through securitizations and derisking. We've prepared for Basel III Endgame impacts via model adjustments and maintain buffers for growth and returns.

On provisions for credit losses, we recorded $450 million, up slightly quarter-over-quarter but down year-over-year, covering our $450 billion portfolio. Consumer drove much of it with credit card delinquencies at 3.2%, C&I saw margin pressures, CRE office exposure prompted reserves amid rising vacancies, and mortgages remained strong. Our CECL approach uses PD, LGD, EAD projections across scenarios, enhanced by machine learning and alt-data for accuracy. ACL covers 2.8x charge-offs, and we expect $420-480 million next quarter.

Revenue diversification has been pivotal, with non-interest income up 22% to $2.8 billion, or 42% of total. Wealth management AUM hit $1.2 trillion on robo-advisory inflows, payments grew via UniPay Nexus platform, and capital markets fees rose on green bonds and trading. These high-margin streams hedge NIM volatility and target 50% mix by 2026.

Finally, our macro view supports this: U.S. consumer resilience with low unemployment aids deposits and loans, Europe benefits from rate dynamics, Asia mixes China caution with India growth, and markets thrive on volatility. We've managed betas, embedded climate risks, and grown digital fees, raising full-year guidance.

Thank you. I'll hand over to Michael.

Michael Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. From a risk management perspective, we are closely monitoring interest rate volatility, commercial real estate exposure, and geopolitical tensions. We are taking proactive steps to mitigate these risks and maintain a strong risk profile, including covenant resets, hedges, and stress testing against oil shocks or GDP slowdowns, ensuring our buffers hold firm.

David Wong:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains exceptionally strong with non-performing loans at 0.98% and net charge-offs at 0.38%. We are actively managing our loan portfolio and remain confident in our ability to navigate the current economic environment. Specifically, the performance of our commercial real estate portfolio has been strong, though monitored closely.

To elaborate on our $450 billion loan portfolio's resilience, we've upheld conservative underwriting through rising rates to the Fed's 5.25-5.50% range. NPL ratio, excluding government guarantees, fell to 98 basis points, down 12 sequentially and 25 year-over-year, our lowest since pre-COVID and below the 1.15% industry average per FDIC. Delinquencies improved to 1.85% from 2.05%, despite high credit card utilization.

Annualized NCOs held at 38 basis points, down from 45 last year, with $420 million in charge-offs offset by provision reversals, leading to $65 million net expense. ACL is 1.42% of loans or 144% of NPLs, ample for recession scenarios.

By segment: Consumer at 45% of portfolio saw NPLs drop to 65 basis points on employment strength, credit cards at 2.1% delinquencies, autos slightly higher but aided by telematics. C&I at 30% edged to 1.45% NPLs from cyclical sectors, with low NCOs and de-risking in sponsored finance. CRE at 20% steady at 1.80% NPLs but delinquencies up to 2.75%, focused on multifamily/industrial in Sun Belt, office minimal at 8%. Residential at 5% pristine at 45 basis points NPLs.

Regionally, Southeast and Midwest unemployment at 3.6% helps, versus Northeast CRE softness. Initiatives like AI Sentinel platform cut delinquencies 15% via predictive scoring, CECL enhancements with Fed data, CRE securitizations trimming $2.5 billion, and higher FICO originations. We see NPLs stabilizing at 90-100 basis points, NCOs 35-45, with buffers for downside.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our technology initiatives. We are making significant progress on our digital transformation, including the launch of our AI-powered mobile banking app which has seen over 500,000 new users and 20% increase in digital transactions in terms of customer adoption and efficiency gains. This builds on cloud migrations, GenAI for fraud and personalization, real-time payments, and blockchain pilots, driving down costs and upping uptime.

Robert Kline:
Good morning. We are focused on operational excellence and driving efficiency across the organization. Key initiatives include process automation and branch optimization, which are contributing to improved productivity and cost savings, alongside customer loyalty programs and ESG-aligned lending.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson:
Good morning. Can you provide further insights into your loan growth outlook?

John Reynolds:
Thanks, Mike. Our loan growth remains disciplined, targeting 6-8% for the year, focused on high-quality C&I in tech and renewables, consumer via digital channels, and selective CRE in growth markets. We've got a robust pipeline, supported by deposit inflows and macro resilience, while maintaining FICO 740+ standards. This aligns with our CET1 strength for balanced expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
What are your plans for capital return plans?

Sarah Chen:
Hi Emily. With CET1 at 13.2%, we're committing $1.2 billion to buybacks this year and hiking the dividend 65 basis points to $0.48 per share, at a 95% payout ratio. Next year targets $4-5 billion total returns, balancing M&A like fintech bolt-ons and organic growth. Basel preparations keep us flexible above our 250 basis point buffer.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Tom Lee:
How are you managing credit risk in CRE?

Michael Patel:
Good question, Tom. CRE is 20% of loans, skewed to multifamily and industrial in Sun Belt areas with attractive cap rates. Office is just 8% or $12 billion, stress-tested to 200 bps expansion. We've trimmed high-LTV via $2.5 billion securitizations, built interest reserves, and use AI early warnings. Delinquencies up modestly but NCOs minimal, with regional diversification aiding.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kim:
Can you discuss the performance of digital transformation efforts?

David Wong:
Certainly, Sarah. Our digital push, including Sentinel AI on 500+ variables and Plaid integrations, has reduced delinquencies 15%, sped CECL modeling, and grown digital users 18% to 14.2 million. Mobile deposits at 62% of inflows, RTP payments up 180%, and robo-advisory AUM surging, all lifting NIM and fees while cutting costs 28%.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to John Reynolds for any closing remarks.

John Reynolds:
Thank you for your interest in Horizon Financial Group. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
